cards.question: What is interior mutability?
cards.answer: It lets you mutate a value through a shared (read) reference. Normally the type system forbids an active read while a write exists to the same value.

cards.question: How does Cell mutate without aliasing UB?
cards.answer: Cell only lets you copy T if T is Copy, or replace T. It is single-threaded.

cards.question: Why can Cell aliases observe a change that &i32 cannot?
cards.answer: Rust forbids &T and &mut T to the same value, so a write through b cannot change a. Two &Cell<i32> can point at the same cell, so a later get can differ.

cards.question: What does Cell::take do for a non-Copy T?
cards.answer: It replaces the inner value with the default (an empty Vec in the example) and returns the old value so you can mutate and set it back.

cards.question: How does RefCell enforce aliasing?
cards.answer: It tracks a borrow count at runtime. Taking a mutable borrow while shared borrows exist, or the reverse, panics.

cards.question: Can Cell or RefCell be sent across threads?
cards.answer: No. Both are single-threaded and cannot be sent across threads.
